result.title: An Interaction-Aware Decision Framework for FDIC-Assisted Distressed Bank Acquisitions: Empirical Evidence from the FDIC Failed-Bank Panel and the SVB-First Citizens Case
result.comment: 18 pages, 2 figures, 15 tables. Research code, datasets, and reproducibility materials are available at https://github.com/malihealiasgari20/FDIC-SNFF-Decision-Framework
result.summary: Acquirers of failed banks weigh acquisition value, regulatory protection, risk, buyer strength, and execution difficulty jointly, because each signal's meaning depends on the others: high non-performing loans matter less when government loss sharing absorbs the losses. The proposed Spider Network Filtering Framework encodes such dependencies as four interpretable interaction rules among five dimensions, yielding graph-inspired features for a logistic model and a Pursue/Caution/Avoid decision rule. We evaluate it on 55 acquisitions assisted by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation in 2008-2024 by acquirers with a parent listed in the United States. Six financial inputs come from regulatory reports published before each failure; two deal terms, which the winning bidder knows when it bids but investors learn at the announcement, come from the regulator's press releases. The outcome, a positive three-day abnormal return around the announcement, records the market's initial reception, not realized success. Under grouped, nested cross-validation, the Spider-enhanced model reaches a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.594, against 0.615 for logistic regression on the same inputs and 0.632 for ridge regression; permutation tests that repeat the full model selection give at most weak evidence that any of them ranks better than chance. The Spider score used directly does not rank better than chance, and an apparent link between target distress and higher returns disappears against a bank-sector benchmark. Thresholds tuned for the F1 score approve most acquisitions with negative returns and realize negative utility when each costs three times what a positively received acquisition gains.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 Spider Network Filtering Framework，把五个维度的交互规则编码为图特征并接入逻辑回归，用于判断是否收购 FDIC 接管的困境银行，并在 55 例交易上做交叉验证评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 属金融并购决策与表格数据分类研究，不涉及视觉或多模态表示、latent 推理状态、证据筛选或停止决策，其交互规则与可解释特征构造也未提供可核查的 LVR 方法线索，故排除。
